findings.problem: status: String allows any arbitrary string value (e.g. "banana", "", null-byte payloads) making illegal shard states representable
findings.failure_mode: Downstream code cannot exhaustively match on status; invalid or unexpected status strings pass silently through validation gates
findings.fix: Replace String with a sealed ShardStatus enum { Pending, Validated, Sent } with no Default and no FromStr impl for untrusted input

findings.problem: is_validated: bool is a lifecycle boolean that can be independently toggled from other fields, enabling impossible state combinations (validated=false, is_sent=true, sent_at_epoch_ms=Some)
findings.failure_mode: A shard could be marked sent without ever being validated, or validated after being sent, violating workflow invariants
findings.fix: Collapse into a typestate enum where Validated and Sent are distinct variants; Sent variant carries sent_at_epoch_ms

findings.problem: is_sent: bool is a lifecycle boolean independently mutable from is_validated, creating unbounded state space (2^3 = 8 combinations vs 3 valid transitions)
findings.failure_mode: Any boolean combination of is_validated and is_sent is representable, including sent-then-validated reversal
findings.fix: Merge is_validated and is_sent into a single typestate enum with ordered variants and transitions only

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is a bare optional field on the struct, decoupled from the lifecycle state it semantically belongs to
findings.failure_mode: sent_at_epoch_ms can be Some while is_sent is false, or None while is_sent is true; the optional leaks lifecycle data outside the state machine
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms into the Sent variant of the typestate enum as a non-optional u64, carrying the timestamp only when valid

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive that cannot distinguish shard IDs from other strings (names, paths, tokens)
findings.failure_mode: Accidental reuse of non-ID strings as shard IDs; no validation or uniqueness enforcement at the type level
findings.fix: Introduce a nonEmptyShardId newtype (struct NonEmptyShardId(String)) with a smart constructor that validates non-empty at construction

findings.problem: mark_sent takes a fully mutable ShardWorkflow and mutates status string, is_sent bool, and leaves is_validated and sent_at_epoch_ms untouched, enabling arbitrary state mutation without validation of preconditions
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can transition a shard to sent without checking validated flag, without recording timestamp, and without preventing reversal
findings.fix: Replace with a pure function: fn try_transition_to_sent(shard: &ShardWorkflow) -> Result<ShardWorkflow, ShardError> that requires Validated state as precondition and returns typed error otherwise

findings.problem: No error type defined; mark_sent returns ShardWorkflow with no failure signal for invalid transitions
findings.failure_mode: Failed transitions are silently swallowed; callers cannot distinguish success from ignored failure
findings.fix: Define enum ShardError { NotValidated, AlreadySent } and return Result<ShardWorkflow, ShardError>

findings.problem: No private constructor or smart constructor; ShardWorkflow is a public struct with all pub fields, allowing external construction of invalid state in a single expression
findings.failure_mode: External code can construct ShardWorkflow with id="", status="", is_validated=false, is_sent=true, sent_at_epoch_ms=Some(0) — every invariant violated simultaneously
findings.fix: Make all fields private; provide ShardWorkflow::new(id: NonEmptyShardId) -> ShardWorkflow for the initial Pending state; no other construction path

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent performance on ShardWorkflow
no allocation analysis: mark_sent clones ShardWorkflow by value on every call, creating redundant String allocations for id and status on each transition
no profiler evidence that the 3-field mutation (status, is_sent, sent_at_epoch_ms) is the measured bottleneck vs the typestate redesign
no command-truth evidence: cargo fmt --check, cargo check, cargo clippy with strict gates not run
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The entire ShardWorkflow type is architecturally unsound: it makes every illegal state representable, has no error signaling, no lifecycle enforcement, and no smart constructors. The mark_sent function is a no-op guard — it sets fields without validation. A full redesign to a typestate enum with a pure transition function is required before any performance work.
